html:
From February to April 1804, on the orders of Dessalines, soldiers in newly independent Haiti killed most of the French men, women and children who had stayed on. Several thousand people died.

Dessalines saw the French as a threat who might help Napoleon try again to restore slavery. Some groups were spared, among them Polish soldiers who had deserted the French army, and German settlers.

Slave owners in the United States and Europe used the killings as proof that freeing slaves led to slaughter. The massacre added to the isolation of Haiti in its first decades, alongside the independence debt that followed the declaration of independence.
